C.title: Parent lease copies and legacy borrow release share one lifetime
C.problem: Current exported DataRootLease value contains mutex, file and borrowed flag directly. External code can copy the value without touching private fields. Revision03 explicitly protects borrow copies but does not explicitly protect parent copies or distinguish old ReturnBorrow from the new maintenance borrower. A copied parent could Close its copied state while a maintenance borrower is active; a reused boolean could let ReturnBorrow clear the wrong borrow.
C.required: Make every DataRootLease value point to one private heap owner-state containing mutex, file, generation, closed state and active borrow identity/kind. Copies, Root/Held/Close, old Borrow/ReturnBorrow and new Maintenance methods must consult that same state. Nil/zero parent and borrow must fail closed without panic. Legacy ReturnBorrow may release only an active legacy coordinator borrow; it must reject an active maintenance borrow. Maintenance Release consumes only its exact private generation-bound token, and cannot release a later or legacy borrow. Parent Close refuses either live borrow and invalidates all copies atomically on successful close. No lock held while recursively calling a method that takes it.
tests: Copy parent before borrow; copied Close refuses and original Held remains true.
Copy parent/borrow; release one borrow; stale copy cannot release a newly acquired borrow.
Legacy ReturnBorrow during maintenance borrow fails and cannot enable Close; concurrent legacy/maintenance borrow admits only one.
Zero-value Close/Check/Borrow never panics and never claims Held.

C.title: One normalization and identity guard across all upgrade branches
C.problem: All five plans enter the new adapter, but queue/configuration branches call upgradePaths again and then open templates/source later. Merely retaining coordinator.lock and checking a path at adapter entry does not stop a source/root rename or alias change before a downstream open. The text requires revalidation after normalization but does not place it in these existing common call sites.
C.required: Within the existing allowed backup_upgrade.go, make the shared upgradePaths path finish by validating opt.sourceLease against the final normalized root/source for guarded production workflows, before returning to any branch. The private adapter/source borrow must retain native no-delete/rename guards for the exact root path components and source file identity until all downstream DB defers complete; metadata handles may share read/write needed by SQLite but cannot permit identity replacement. Check canonical containment, no reparse and exact native file identities. Existing prepared wrapper Check remains required. Public UpgradeLocal/UpgradePreparedAbandonmentBackup stay fail-closed before any provider/key/template/store work. Isolated private legacy algorithm fixtures cannot count as guarded entry proof. This selected central implementation avoids adding queue/configuration production files; if the builder cannot implement these persistent guards, STOP and request an exact scope addition for explicit checks, rather than omit the invariant.
tests: Exercise every five-plan dispatch using a real held lease, including normalized option copy.
Attempt source file/root component replacement after adapter borrow and before template/source open; deny replacement or fail before forbidden setup.
Prepared nested local/handoff inner Close/error leaves outer Held and cannot release the native owner.
Forbidden Canary/key/provider/template/store sentinel remains untouched for invalid plans, wrong identity and pending journals.

C.title: Exact-own recovery validates the pending transition, not only prior terminal target
C.problem: Replacement can die after ReplaceFile while journal remains PUBLISHING and target already equals NewBytes. Applying ordinary history-current/latest-terminal-target comparison before granting its exact own inspection permit would reject this legitimate recovery. Treating the permit as a broad pending exemption would create the opposite flaw.
C.required: Freeze two separate pure predicates in the shared reader: ordinary acquisition validates complete history and current terminal target; exact-own inspection validates the full causal history including the one exact pending operation and its permitted current old/new state using the existing replacementRecover applied/unapplied evidence predicates. Include exact namespace/root/operation/plan digest and bounded file inventory. PREPARED/PUBLISHING partial histories may enter only the exact recovery inspection that existing recovery rules permit; no ordinary lease or backup borrow may pass. The other namespace and every non-own pending operation always deny. PUBLISHING with exact applied NewBytes may be inspected/completed; it cannot abort or replay ReplaceFile. Unknown/mixed/tampered backup/stage/hash evidence denies. C own inspection must similarly preserve its existing NOT_APPLIED/ABORTED rules. Revalidate under the held lock; no serialized permit, callback, bool or raw handle supplies authority.
tests: Both PUBLISHING-before-ReplaceFile and PUBLISHING-after-ReplaceFile retain the exact existing recovery result.
A prior completed replacement followed by pending own replacement never requires target to remain predecessor bytes once own publish applied.
Own C permit cannot exempt replacement; own replacement cannot exempt C; backup borrow rejects both exceptions.
Unknown inventory, wrong plan/root/operation, concurrent second pending entry and changed target all fail closed.
